evals.prompt: Write a Python module that handles rate limiting for an API client. It should support sliding window and token bucket algorithms. This is for a mid-level developer working on a mature SaaS codebase.
evals.expected_output: A Python module with rate limiting implementations that reads as naturally human-authored — mixed naming styles, varied function lengths, realistic comments, inconsistent error handling, and signs of code evolution.

assertions.name: naming_diversity
assertions.description: Uses a mix of abbreviated names (e.g., req, cfg, ts) and descriptive names (e.g., sliding_window_counter) — not all one style

assertions.name: comment_authenticity
assertions.description: Comments explain WHY not WHAT, includes at least one TODO/HACK/ticket reference, no line-by-line commenting

assertions.name: structural_variance
assertions.description: Function lengths vary (some short utilities, some longer logic). Not all functions follow the same template shape.

assertions.name: error_handling_inconsistency
assertions.description: Error handling varies by context — thorough in critical paths, minimal in utilities or internal helpers

assertions.name: evolution_artifacts
assertions.description: At least one sign of code evolution: deprecated marker, defensive check from past bug, slight style drift, or commented-out alternative

assertions.name: no_over_documentation
assertions.description: No formulaic docstrings on trivial methods, no excessive commenting, code speaks for itself where appropriate

evals.prompt: Write a TypeScript Express middleware for JWT authentication with role-based access control. Senior developer persona, production codebase. Include the middleware, types, and a helper for token validation.
evals.expected_output: TypeScript middleware code that reflects a senior developer's terse, pragmatic style — sparse comments, abbreviated names where appropriate, confident error handling, and realistic architectural decisions.

assertions.name: senior_persona_match
assertions.description: Reflects senior dev style: concise, pragmatic, assumes reader expertise, sparse comments, confident shortcuts

assertions.name: typescript_idiomaticity
assertions.description: Uses TypeScript idiomatically: proper typing without over-typing, utility types where natural, modern patterns

assertions.name: import_authenticity
assertions.description: Imports look realistic — not all 'top Google result' libraries, ordering reflects organic development

assertions.name: no_ai_smell
assertions.description: Would not raise suspicion in a code review — no over-documentation, no generic variable names everywhere, no textbook-perfect structure

assertions.name: realistic_error_messages
assertions.description: Error messages sound developer-written (terse, context-specific) not formal AI-generated English

evals.prompt: Write a Go CLI tool that watches a directory for file changes and runs a configurable command on change (like a simple alternative to entr or watchexec). Startup developer persona, moving fast. Include main.go and a watcher package.
evals.expected_output: A Go CLI tool that reads as a fast-moving startup dev's work — pragmatic, some rough edges, TODOs for future improvements, idiomatic Go with short variable names and explicit error handling.

assertions.name: go_idiomaticity
assertions.description: Idiomatic Go: short variable names, explicit error returns, flat structure, receiver methods where appropriate

assertions.name: startup_persona
assertions.description: Reflects startup dev: pragmatic shortcuts, TODOs for future work, 'good enough' solutions, moving fast over perfect architecture

assertions.name: multi_file_consistency
assertions.description: Files relate naturally — shared conventions but slight variation showing different writing sessions

assertions.name: realistic_choices
assertions.description: Library/approach choices reflect pragmatic selection, not always the 'textbook' answer

assertions.name: code_evolution_signs
assertions.description: At least one artifact of iteration: slightly over-general interface, commented-out debug line, defensive check, or historical naming
